purpose: Turn documentation sufficiency into repeatable evidence that a reader can complete the documented action and reach the stated result.

prerequisites: Names required product version, browser/schema channel, locale, role, fixture, profile state, API token if relevant, and whether screenshots are required.
Separates source-install prerequisites from packaged-installer or production-service assumptions.
exact_steps: Lists the commands, clicks, API calls, file paths, and form choices in executable order.
Does not hide required setup behind summary phrases such as configure as needed.
Keeps commands copyable and avoids translated command/path/API identifiers.
expected_result: States the observable successful end state: page, saved profile, exported file, validation response, health check, generated artifact, or documented boundary decision.
Includes the exact status, file, route, response field, or UI state needed to confirm success.
recovery_path: Names at least one likely failure mode and the next user action.
Points to troubleshooting content when recovery exceeds the topic's normal scope.
drift_source: Names the product file, inventory, schema, fixture, Make target, API route, DITA map, or external-source policy that can make the topic stale.
Requires a focused rerun command when the drift source changes.
focused_verification: Uses the narrowest relevant docs contract, product unit, API, browser, command, or simulation check before release gates.
Records what remains unverified when browser, OS, network, or distribution access is not used.

hands_on_browser.description: A maintainer performs the documented UI workflow with deterministic test state.
hands_on_browser.artifact: test name, screenshot report, or short review note under the approved reports boundary

hands_on_command_transcript.description: A maintainer runs the documented shell/API commands in a disposable environment.
hands_on_command_transcript.artifact: sanitized command transcript, focused test log, or review note

browser_smoke.description: A committed browser test executes the representative path.

api_or_unit_test.description: A committed unit/API/contract test executes the documented boundary.

static_source_simulation.description: A deterministic source/fixture comparison proves commands, routes, keys, examples, and expected states without running the external system.
static_source_simulation.artifact: fixture path, compared source path, and focused test command

documented_simulation_evidence.description: A written simulation explains why hands-on execution is unavailable and maps every step to deterministic source, fixture, or test evidence.
documented_simulation_evidence.artifact: review record with assumptions, unverified boundary, and release-blocking follow-up if the simulation is insufficient

explicit_waiver.description: A maintainer-approved non-goal or unavailable environment decision.
explicit_waiver.artifact: dated waiver record with owner and release impact

user-guide.scope: All user-visible task topics and troubleshooting topics that instruct a user to operate BPM.
user-guide.closure_rule: A User Guide task cannot close from topic presence or static coverage alone; it needs hands-on execution, browser smoke, or documented simulation evidence.

firefox-policy-guide.scope: Policy and managed-preference reference topics, channel notes, examples, validation caveats, and related user tasks.
firefox-policy-guide.closure_rule: Reference topics may close with source-backed simulation when the policy cannot be safely applied in a live browser.

cis-settings-guide.scope: CIS orientation, selection, preset/layer merge, manual-review, deviation, verification, and workflow topics.
cis-settings-guide.closure_rule: CIS topics must prove BPM behavior and source-attribution boundaries without copying restricted benchmark expression.

administrator-guide.scope: Source deployment, operations, updates, API integration, troubleshooting, and production-readiness boundaries.
administrator-guide.closure_rule: Administrator source-install tasks cannot close from static text checks alone; they require hands-on command execution or documented simulation evidence.

must_include: exact distribution or OS name and version
exit status or observable result for each verification command
unverified external boundary if simulation was used
blocked_if_missing: database migration or explicit no-migration statement

review_records.storage: documentation/reports/diagnostics/ for disposable local review notes, or docs/architecture/ for accepted release-blocking sufficiency records.

manual_or_simulation_required_for: five selected Linux distribution command topics

non_goals: This protocol does not perform the sufficiency review.
This protocol does not select the five Linux distributions.
This protocol does not add or rewrite DITA topics.
This protocol does not hand-edit generated HTML, manifests, search indexes, or installed app/documentation/site artifacts.
